_note: DESIGN-TBD: prices and most tier counts are placeholders (OPEN_QUESTIONS §4), except the dash, whose four total tiers are the owner's prices of October 17, 2026 (USER_REQUESTS.md; no longer placeholders): 300 (tier I), 450 (II), 600 (III) and 700 (IV), so a player can own it before the first boss, and it is the first item in this list and so the first card in the shop. GDD §8 fixes the weapon's four tiers. R7 laid these prices against tools/measure/economy.gd's reading of the post-playtest economy (G1 pace, G3 free armor, G4 laser tier 1); I7 rebalanced them for all eight zones (GDD §7, the owner's answer of October 14, 2026): each tier is read at its line total (its price and every tier before it, since tiers are bought in order) against the wallet of a typical player who finishes every level once, and test_economy.gd pins the level each tier first fits at (the table is in docs/architecture/economy-platforms.md). A tier that first fits at level N is affordable after finishing N, so usable from N + 1. Held: Armor I 350 (the October 3 early-economy revision) and Laser I 1800 (first affordable at the campaign's 4th level, Gangland 1). Moved: Armor IV 6000 to 6500 and Heavy missile 9500 to 7000, which I4's treasure-stash credits had pulled too early; see items 846-850 in docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS*.md.

_cosmetics_note: The shop's Cosmetics section (GDD §8, 'Cosmetics'; the owner, October 18, 2026): looks for the runner, bought once with credits from the same wallet and kept forever; the player picks one to wear. They never change gameplay. 'default_cosmetic' is Razor Echo's own look, free and always owned. 'cosmetics' are the outfits in shop order; each id names its outfit file (scripts/player/outfits/<id>.gd, PlayerOutfits), and an id with no file yet wears a tinted placeholder of Echo's base look in 'color' (PlayerOutfits.placeholder_parts). Cosmetics are not in 'items': the economy tools and tests price items only. Rex and Camo (3,000 each) are the owner's prices. DESIGN-TBD: Beach Master (meant to be won by completing challenges), Centurion (the prize for winning the weekly seed) and Party Wolf (the reward for promoting the game) are sold for 5,000 credits for now, a placeholder so they aren't forgotten, until those ways of winning them are designed (docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS*.md item 979).
